title: Metallic Gross-Neveu criticality and superconductivity on the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ SLAC fermion
authors: Feng-Yu Zhang, Yin-Kai Yu, Zi-Xiang Li, Shuai Yin
abstract: The realization of Dirac criticality beyond the conventional Gross-Neveu-Yukawa (GNY) paradigm has become a major frontier in condensed matter physics. In this work, we introduce an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-symmetric bilayer SLAC fermion model with tunable inter-layer interactions that exhibits a rich quantum phase diagram. As the interaction strength increases, the system undergoes two distinct phase transitions. The primary transition is a continuous boundary separating a Dirac semimetal (DSM) from an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-broken ordered phase. Crucially, this transition evades the standard GNY universality class because the emergent order only gaps out a subset of the itinerant fermions. Using large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations, we establish that this transition belongs to the Gross-Neveu-$\mathrm{SO}(3)$ universality class with $N=6$ irreducible Dirac cones and precisely extract the corresponding critical exponents. At stronger couplings, a second transition drives the system into an inter-layer $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-symmetric superconducting (SC) state. We provide strong numerical evidence that this transition is a quantum-fluctuation-driven first-order transition. Our study provides new insights into the exploration of Dirac criticality beyond the standard GNY universality class, and also offers a novel platform to realize superconductivity featuring $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry.
summary: This work analyzes an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-symmetric bilayer SLAC fermion model to explore its quantum phase diagram. Using QMC simulations, the authors identify a continuous transition into an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-broken metallic state, followed by a distinct first-order transition into a novel superconducting phase. This provides new insights into Dirac criticality and unconventional superconductivity.
main_problem: The study investigates Dirac criticality beyond standard universality classes and explores novel superconducting states within an interacting fermion model.
main_result: The system exhibits a continuous phase transition belonging to the Gross-Neveu-$\mathrm{SO}(3)$ class, followed by a strong-coupling first-order quantum phase transition into an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-symmetric superconducting state.
method: Large-scale Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations and Finite-Size Scaling (FSS) analysis were used to extract critical exponents and characterize the nature of the phase transitions.
model_or_system: The model is an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-symmetric bilayer SLAC fermion system in $d=2$ dimensions, described by a Hamiltonian with tunable inter-layer interactions ($J$).

main_assumptions: The QMC method is used to probe ground-state expectation values, and comparisons are made between QMC results (suggesting first-order transitions) and mean-field HFB calculations (suggesting continuous coexistence).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing the sequence of transitions; specific plots show data collapse for critical exponents and the abrupt onset of superconducting order parameters at strong coupling.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system's behavior across increasing interaction strength $J$: first, characterizing the continuous transition to an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-broken phase using QMC; second, investigating the nature of the subsequent strong-coupling instability into a superconducting state by comparing various pairing channels.
why_interesting: The study provides concrete numerical evidence for exotic critical points and superconductivity in strongly interacting fermions, which is highly relevant to understanding unconventional superconductors and quantum criticality beyond simple BCS theory.
